newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says south Lebanon ally behind shelling.
newsitem.headline: Israel says south Lebanon ally behind shelling.

text.p: Israel said forces under the command of its south Lebanon militia ally Antoine Lahd were responsible for the shelling on Monday of the port city of Sidon in which six civilians were killed and 36 were wounded.
"Israel did not, I repeat did not, fire on Sidon today," Israel's chief military spokesman, Brigadier-General Oded Ben-Ami, told reporters.

He said the shelling was carried out from the Jezzine area, just north of an Israeli-held occupation zone patrolled by Israeli soldiers and Lahd's South Lebanon Army (SLA), and that Israel was against the targeting of civilians.

"We are coordinated absolutely with the SLA inside the security zone in Lebanon in the south. The Jezzine area is out of this area. General Lahd has his forces in the Jezzine area as well...out of our responsibility, out of our control," he said.

The attack, the first time Sidon had been shelled since a major Israeli military offensive in April 1996, followed the killing of three Lebanese youths in the Jezzine area when a roadside bomb blew up their vehicle.

Ben-Ami identified two of the youths as the 11-year-old daughter and 17-year-old son of Lahd's late commander in Jezzine, Assad Nasr. He said Hizbollah, the Iranian-backed "Party of God", carried out the attack.
The Israeli news agency Itim quoted Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai as saying he regretted the targeting of civilians in Lebanon and would use "all his influence" to halt such attacks.
Ben-Ami said the Israeli military would urge Lahd not to violate a ceasefire agreement that ended Israel's 1996 offensive with an understanding by the parties to the conflict not to target civilians.
"We are absolutely against the loss of civilians and against targeting civilians no matter what part of Lebanon they are living in," Ben-Ami said.

Israel and its SLA allies patrol a 15-km (nine-mile) deep border zone set up inside Lebanon with the declared aim of preventing guerrilla attacks on Israel's northern border. They often engage in fierce clashes with Hizbollah fighters.

Shortly after Monday's shelling subsided, Katyusha rockets struck Jezzine and Marjayoun in south Lebanon, where Israeli forces and the SLA maintain their headquarters. Pro-Israeli militia sources in Lebanon said the rocket attacks killed a 60-year-old civilian man and wounded two women in Jezzine.
The head of Israel's northern command, Amiram Levine, urged Hizbollah not to strike at northern Israel.
"We are doing our utmost not to hit civilians and I hope and advise Hizbollah not to make a mistake and try to hit Israeli civilians," Levine told reporters.
